newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate plunges at close on liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate plunges at close on liquidity.

text.p: Mexican secondary money market rates ended sharply down on Wednesday as local and foreign buyers continued to flood the market, traders said.
Overnight Cetes rates ended down 150 basis points at 22.75 percent.

"The market is still bullish and very liquid, which is matched with a strong peso and so rates are coming down" a trader said. Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed down 185 basis points at 23.50 percent.
Foreign capital inflow buoyed up the benchmark 48-hour peso to close 1.1 centavos firmer at 7.8220/7.8270 per dollar.
Dealers said demand for money market paper was driven by expectations that domestic inflation would fall in the medium term.
"Although we expect December inflation figures to be high, longer term prospects are good so buyers are still in the market," a dealer said.
Banco de Mexico is due to publish December inflation data on Thursday.
Liquidity shortages caused by credit maturities totaling 1.648 billion pesos were outweighed during the session by government spending and cash returning to the system after the weekend.

In view of this situation, Banco de Mexico took the unusual step of draining 199 million pesos in surplus liquidity from the market by an overnight purchase of paper at 23.41 percent. Total maturities estimated for Thursday were estimated at 1.052 billion pesos.
